The CNIL report suggests that the design of algorithmic systems can empower users by promoting a design that enhances autonomy and reflexivity, allowing individuals to make informed decisions. This involves creating systems that provide better information and visualization tools, enabling users to understand the recommendations made by algorithms and to test different responses based on varying parameters.

An example given to illustrate this is the "Politoscope," developed by the Institut des Systèmes Complexes de Paris-Île de France. This tool allows the public to explore large datasets and see the activity and strategies of political communities on social networks, thereby helping to counterbalance the influence of algorithms and giving users more control over the information they receive.
